result:
Honest answer first: I don't have desires or lived experience the way a person does, so this is a considered pick rather than a heartfelt wish. If I had one lever, I'd make sure every person's basic needs were reliably met — food, clean water, shelter, medicine, and education.

Partly because it's concrete enough to act on, and partly because so many other problems cascade from scarcity and insecurity: conflict, exploitation, preventable disease, kids pulled out of school. When people aren't in survival mode, they can learn, create, take risks, and look after each other.

It wouldn't be a single switch — it'd mean changing incentives, institutions, and how abundance gets shared. But as "one way," it's the change that unlocks the most other changes.
